newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Bank of China set to shine.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Bank of China set to shine.

text.p: For the second day in a row, China provided welcome relief in a market sunk in a summertime torpor.
Bank of China launched a HK$2 billion floating-rate certificate of deposit (FRCD) issue through sole arranger China Development Finance Co's Hong Kong branch.
The FRCDs were issued at par, carrying a coupon of 31 basis points over the one-month Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate.
Bankers expected the issue, which straddles the handover, to "fly out the window". Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule on July 1 and bank responses are due back on July 3.

"I would have thought it's fairly clear everybody's going to go in. Now the extent to which people go in will depend on whether there's the carrot out there of a possible cutback (in case of a massive Oversubscription)," said one banker contemplating the issue.
"But at this pricing, it will be awfully tempting for Bank of China to take as much as it can get," he added.
The all-in at the top level is 36 basis points for HK$200 million or more.
A banker with a Japanese institution said the pricing but added: "If It's Bank of China we will be sure to join."
But a senior syndicate manager with a local bank said the all-in was reasonable given the 36-38 basis point secondary market price range of Bank of China's last five-year deal.
"It's (also) borrowing at an auspicious time," he added, referring to the handover.

Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corp's three-year issue in May, which was issued at par to float at 20 basis points over one-month HIBOR, and Bank of East Asia's FRCD was priced to float at 30 basis points over HIBOR.
If last October's FRCD by Bank of China is any guide, Friday's issue should be a stunning success.
Also a HK$2 billion five-year issue with no puts or calls, it was doubled to HK$4 billion after being oversubscribed 4.5 times in syndication.
The October deal featured an all-in of 41.5 basis points, slightly higher than the Friday's deal.
In other news, the Philippines launched its US$500 million Yankee overnight in two tranches: US$400 million for 30 years, and the remainder for 100 years.
Issue price was 99.908 for the 30-year tranche, with a 184.9 basis point spread over treasuries, while the 100-year tranche was issued at 98.459 and priced at 197.5 basis points.
Cheju Island, a Korean tourist resort may launch about 20 billion yen 10 samurai bonds next week.
Korea Telecom is expected to close its US$100 million loan early in July, bankers said.
The loan pays an interest margin of 45 basis oints over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate
The Philippine central bank raised rates after spillover nervousness from Thailand's economic woes rattled the peso.
The Thai government is grappling with measures to guide the country out of its worst economic crisis in over a decade.
On Friday, it named a new finance minister -- its sixth since 1995 in three administrations -- after the resignation of Amnuay Viravan.
